description: The declared-vs-actual return-type check on scalar LANGUAGE SQL UDFs at CREATE time, live-verified cell by cell: incompatibility is decided by type FAMILY (fixed vs floating point split, each timestamp flavor its own, VARIANT/ARRAY/OBJECT match only themselves, BOOLEAN/TIME/BINARY their own), parameters never matter (narrowing accepted), a body cast changes the verdict, a NULL body matches anything, parameter references carry their declared types, a single-item FROM-less SELECT body is checked like an expression, and neither procedures nor JavaScript handlers are checked. The refusal is the bare sentence Declared return type 'X' is incompatible with actual return type 'Y' with parameters spelled on both sides. Converted 1:1 from ddl/UdfReturnTypeCompatibilityTest (now retired).
